findings.where: First screen, the 'Placeholder: Mark's photo…' caption: on desktop at the bottom left under the action column; on phone below the action, a full screen-height away from the photo at the top
findings.fault: The caption is placed by the text column, not by the photograph it describes. Because it is far from the photo, it reads as a loose footnote to the page or to the email action rather than as the photo's label.
findings.who_objects: The founder judging the first screen. The caption exists to mark the photo as a stand-in, but here it reads as page text. Once real photos replace these, the visitor gets the same caption arrangement with the caption cut off from its image.

findings.where: Article specimen, desktop: the designer's notes column ('Text on a 32 px line…', 'Grey for reading, blue only…') to the right of the article title
findings.fault: The specimen has no frame or ground of its own that separates it from the tile. The builder's notes sit at the top right of the article in its sidebar position, so they read as part of the article page (a sidebar or pull note) rather than as notes about it. It is not clear where the article page starts and ends.
findings.who_objects: The founder, and later Angélique, reading the specimen as the article page a visitor would see. They could take the rhythm notes for page content and misjudge how busy an article page is.

findings.where: Article specimen, the lecture PDF row under the article (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The lecture title and its 'Lecture · 23 April 2026' line are indented a few pixels in from the article's left edge, so the text no longer lines up with the paragraphs and list above it.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader, or Mark himself. The brief makes this PDF list 'the product', and on a page whose case is precision, a slipped edge right under the article looks careless.

findings.where: Texture section, desktop: the two photographs and the text under them fill only the left half; the right half of the 1100 px column is empty
findings.fault: Every other section spans the full column or balances two columns. This one leaves a large dead area on the right, so it looks unfinished next to its neighbours.
findings.who_objects: The founder scanning the style tile. The section looks unfinished, which weakens the tile's case that the page is considered throughout.

findings.where: Type pair section, desktop: the Newsreader description (left) and the Public Sans description (right)
findings.fault: The two side-by-side descriptions start at different heights: the sans paragraph sits about 30 px above the serif one. The pair is meant to be compared row for row but does not line up.
findings.who_objects: The founder comparing the two faces. The misaligned columns make the pair look loosely assembled, in the section that argues for careful type.
